def update_penalty_weights_and_voxel_goals( model: gurobipy._model.Model, optimization_configs: List[Optimization_Config]): 
715def update_penalty_weights_and_voxel_goals(
716    model: Model,
717    optimization_configs: List["Optimization_Config"],
718):
719    r"""
720    ### Purpose:
721    - Sets penalty weights and per-voxel target dose for every structure in `optimization_configs`,
722    reading every numeric value (weights, `dose_voxel_goal`, `min_dose`, `max_dose`, `hotspot_threshold`,
723    `num_dose_points`, `hotspot_num_dose_points`, `hotspot_masks`) straight from each
724    `Optimization_Config`. NO handles, NO blueprint, NO cached Gurobi object references anywhere:
725    every variable/constraint name is regenerated on the fly from `structure_name` + `num_dose_points`
726    (and, for hotspots, each hotspot mask's name-derived suffix + its own voxel count), then resolved
727    via `model.getVarByName` / a single pass over `model.getQConstrs()`.
728    - Never calls `addVar`/`addConstr`/`remove`: only `Obj`, `QCRHS` and `UB` attributes are mutated,
729    and the objective expression is rebuilt from the resolved `MVar`s. If a structure's weight was 0
730    when `set_penalty_function_and_constraints` ran (so its slack variables were never created), the
731    corresponding name lookup returns `None` and that term is silently skipped - it cannot be added
732    retroactively without calling `set_penalty_function_and_constraints` again.
733
734    ### Performance note:
735    - The original implementation resolved quadratic constraints per-structure by scanning
736    `model.getQConstrs()` once per structure (`O(num_structures * num_qconstrs)`). This version
737    scans `model.getQConstrs()` exactly once for the whole model, parses each constraint's name to
738    determine its type (`c_L`/`c_U`/`c_H`) and owning structure/hotspot-suffix, and drops it into a
739    preallocated slot list resolved via `O(1)` dict lookups. Total constraint-resolution cost is now
740    `O(num_qconstrs + num_structures)` instead of `O(num_structures * num_qconstrs)`. Variable
741    lookups still go through `model.getVarByName` (already `O(1)` per call once the model has been
742    `update()`-d), so `_get_mvar_by_name_indices` is unchanged.
743
744    IMPORTANT: `c_L_*`/`c_U_*`/`c_H_*` are QUADRATIC constraints (bilinear `c_MVar * t_MVar` term), so
745    their RHS is read/written via `QCRHS` (not `RHS`). RHS updates use the bulk
746    `model.setAttr("QCRHS", constr_list, values_list)` form.
747
748    ### Inputs:
749    - `model`: Model := the Gurobi model whose variables/constraints follow the naming convention
750    established by `set_penalty_function_and_constraints`.
751    - `optimization_configs`: List[Optimization_Config] := the current optimization configs. Any of
752    `penalty_weight_linear`, `penalty_weight_quadratic`, `penalty_weight_uniformity`,
753    `penalty_weight_hotspot`, `hotspot_threshold`, `penalty_weight_variance_time`, `dose_voxel_goal`,
754    `min_dose`, `max_dose` can be changed freely between calls.
755    ### Output:
756    - None: `model`'s objective, quadratic constraint QCRHS values, and variable bounds are updated
757    in place. Call `model.optimize()` afterwards as usual.
758    """
759    penalty_terms = {
760        "linear": 0,
761        "quadratic": 0,
762        "uniformity": 0,
763        "hotspot": 0,
764        "dwelltimes": 0,
765    }
766
767    # All dwell-time variables share the "dwell_" name prefix (see CatheterVar_Gurobi). A single scan
768    # of the model's variables is enough to rebuild t_MVar - order doesn't matter here since it only
769    # feeds a mean/variance computation.
770    dwell_vars = [v for v in model.getVars() if v.VarName.startswith("dwell_")]
771    t_MVar = MVar.fromlist(dwell_vars) if dwell_vars else None
772
773    # --- Pass 1 over configs: build lookup structures + preallocate constraint slot lists ---
774    configs_by_structure = {}
775    # structure_name -> {"L": [None]*n, "U": [None]*n or None}
776    constr_slots = {}
777    # hotspot_suffix -> [None]*hs_num
778    hotspot_slots = {}
779
780    for optimization_config in optimization_configs:
781        structure_name = optimization_config.structure_name
782        num_dose_points = optimization_config.num_dose_points
783        if not num_dose_points:
784            continue
785
786        configs_by_structure[structure_name] = optimization_config
787        constr_slots[structure_name] = {
788            "L": [None] * num_dose_points,
789            "U": [None] * num_dose_points if optimization_config.is_target else None,
790        }
791
792        if optimization_config.is_target:
793            hotspot_masks = optimization_config.hotspot_masks or []
794            hotspot_num_dose_points = optimization_config.hotspot_num_dose_points or []
795            for hotspot_mask, hs_num in zip(hotspot_masks, hotspot_num_dose_points):
796                if not hs_num:
797                    continue
798                hotspot_suffix = hotspot_mask.name.split("hotspot_estimator_")[1]
799                hotspot_slots[hotspot_suffix] = [None] * hs_num
800
801    # --- Pass 2: single scan over all quadratic constraints in the model ---
802    for constraint in model.getQConstrs():
803        match = _QCONSTR_NAME_RE.match(constraint.QCName)
804        if match is None:
805            continue
806        ctype, name_part, idx_str = match.groups()
807        idx = int(idx_str)
808
809        if ctype in ("c_L", "c_U"):
810            slots = constr_slots.get(name_part)
811            if slots is None:
812                continue
813            slot_list = slots["L"] if ctype == "c_L" else slots["U"]
814            if slot_list is not None and idx < len(slot_list):
815                slot_list[idx] = constraint
816        else:  # ctype == "c_H"
817            slot_list = hotspot_slots.get(name_part)
818            if slot_list is not None and idx < len(slot_list):
819                slot_list[idx] = constraint
820
821    # --- Pass 3 over configs: resolve variables (O(1) getVarByName calls) and build the objective ---
822    for structure_name, optimization_config in configs_by_structure.items():
823        num_dose_points = optimization_config.num_dose_points
824        min_dose = optimization_config.min_dose
825        max_dose = optimization_config.max_dose
826        voxel_goal = optimization_config.dose_voxel_goal
827        voxel_goal_vec = np.full(num_dose_points, voxel_goal)
828
829        linear_weight = optimization_config.penalty_weight_linear
830        quadratic_weight = optimization_config.penalty_weight_quadratic
831        uniformity_weight = optimization_config.penalty_weight_uniformity
832        penalty_weight_variance_time = optimization_config.penalty_weight_variance_time
833        penalty_weight_hotspot = optimization_config.penalty_weight_hotspot
834        hotspot_threshold = optimization_config.hotspot_threshold
835
836        slots = constr_slots[structure_name]
837        constr_L_raw = slots["L"]
838        constr_L = constr_L_raw if all(c is not None for c in constr_L_raw) else None
839
840        # p_L_/c_L_ is shared naming for both the target dose-slack and the OAR dose-slack (a
841        # structure is either a target or an OAR, never both, so there is no name collision).
842        x_slack = _get_mvar_by_name_indices(model, f"p_L_{structure_name}", num_dose_points)
843
844        if optimization_config.is_target:
845            if x_slack is not None and constr_L is not None:
846                x_slack.UB = np.full(num_dose_points, voxel_goal - min_dose)
847                model.setAttr("QCRHS", constr_L, list(voxel_goal_vec))
848
849                if linear_weight > 0:
850                    penalty_terms["linear"] += (linear_weight / num_dose_points) * x_slack.sum()
851                if quadratic_weight > 0:
852                    penalty_terms["quadratic"] += (quadratic_weight / num_dose_points) * (x_slack @ x_slack)
853
854            constr_U_raw = slots["U"]
855            constr_U = constr_U_raw if constr_U_raw is not None and all(c is not None for c in constr_U_raw) else None
856            y_uniform = _get_mvar_by_name_indices(model, f"p_U_{structure_name}", num_dose_points)
857            if y_uniform is not None and constr_U is not None:
858                y_uniform.UB = np.full(num_dose_points, voxel_goal - min_dose)
859                model.setAttr("QCRHS", constr_U, list(voxel_goal_vec))
860
861                uniformity_coeff = uniformity_weight / num_dose_points * 1e-3
862                penalty_terms["uniformity"] += uniformity_coeff * (y_uniform @ y_uniform)
863
864            # --- hotspot penalty (target structures only, one term per hotspot mask) ---
865            hotspot_masks = optimization_config.hotspot_masks or []
866            hotspot_num_dose_points = optimization_config.hotspot_num_dose_points or []
867            for hotspot_mask, hs_num in zip(hotspot_masks, hotspot_num_dose_points):
868                if not hs_num:
869                    continue
870                hotspot_suffix = hotspot_mask.name.split("hotspot_estimator_")[1]
871                constr_H_raw = hotspot_slots.get(hotspot_suffix)
872                constr_H = constr_H_raw if constr_H_raw is not None and all(c is not None for c in constr_H_raw) else None
873                x_slack_hotspot = _get_mvar_by_name_indices(model, f"p_H_{hotspot_suffix}", hs_num)
874                if x_slack_hotspot is None or constr_H is None:
875                    continue
876
877                model.setAttr("QCRHS", constr_H, [voxel_goal * hotspot_threshold] * hs_num)
878                if penalty_weight_hotspot > 0:
879                    hotspot_coeff = penalty_weight_hotspot / hs_num
880                    penalty_terms["hotspot"] += hotspot_coeff * x_slack_hotspot.sum()
881
882            # --- dwell-time-variance penalty (target structures only, no slack vars involved) ---
883            if penalty_weight_variance_time > 0 and t_MVar is not None:
884                mean_dwell_time = sum(t_MVar) / t_MVar.size
885                penalty_terms["dwelltimes"] += (
886                    penalty_weight_variance_time * 1e-3
887                    * ((t_MVar - mean_dwell_time) @ (t_MVar - mean_dwell_time)) / t_MVar.size
888                )
889        else:
890            if x_slack is not None and constr_L is not None:
891                x_slack.UB = np.full(num_dose_points, max_dose - min_dose)
892                model.setAttr("QCRHS", constr_L, list(voxel_goal_vec))
893
894                if linear_weight > 0:
895                    penalty_terms["linear"] += (linear_weight / num_dose_points) * x_slack.sum()
896                if quadratic_weight > 0:
897                    penalty_terms["quadratic"] += (quadratic_weight / num_dose_points) * (x_slack @ x_slack)
898
899    model.setObjective(
900        penalty_terms["linear"]
901        + penalty_terms["quadratic"]
902        + penalty_terms["uniformity"]
903        + penalty_terms["hotspot"]
904        + penalty_terms["dwelltimes"],
905        GRB.MINIMIZE)
906    model.update()

Purpose:

  • Sets penalty weights and per-voxel target dose for every structure in optimization_configs, reading every numeric value (weights, dose_voxel_goal, min_dose, max_dose, hotspot_threshold, num_dose_points, hotspot_num_dose_points, hotspot_masks) straight from each Optimization_Config. NO handles, NO blueprint, NO cached Gurobi object references anywhere: every variable/constraint name is regenerated on the fly from structure_name + num_dose_points (and, for hotspots, each hotspot mask's name-derived suffix + its own voxel count), then resolved via model.getVarByName / a single pass over model.getQConstrs().
  • Never calls addVar/addConstr/remove: only Obj, QCRHS and UB attributes are mutated, and the objective expression is rebuilt from the resolved MVars. If a structure's weight was 0 when set_penalty_function_and_constraints ran (so its slack variables were never created), the corresponding name lookup returns None and that term is silently skipped - it cannot be added retroactively without calling set_penalty_function_and_constraints again.

Performance note:

  • The original implementation resolved quadratic constraints per-structure by scanning model.getQConstrs() once per structure (O(num_structures * num_qconstrs)). This version scans model.getQConstrs() exactly once for the whole model, parses each constraint's name to determine its type (c_L/c_U/c_H) and owning structure/hotspot-suffix, and drops it into a preallocated slot list resolved via O(1) dict lookups. Total constraint-resolution cost is now O(num_qconstrs + num_structures) instead of O(num_structures * num_qconstrs). Variable lookups still go through model.getVarByName (already O(1) per call once the model has been update()-d), so _get_mvar_by_name_indices is unchanged.

IMPORTANT: c_L_*/c_U_*/c_H_* are QUADRATIC constraints (bilinear c_MVar * t_MVar term), so their RHS is read/written via QCRHS (not RHS). RHS updates use the bulk model.setAttr("QCRHS", constr_list, values_list) form.

Inputs:

  • model: Model := the Gurobi model whose variables/constraints follow the naming convention established by set_penalty_function_and_constraints.

  • optimization_configs: List[Optimization_Config] := the current optimization configs. Any of penalty_weight_linear, penalty_weight_quadratic, penalty_weight_uniformity, penalty_weight_hotspot, hotspot_threshold, penalty_weight_variance_time, dose_voxel_goal, min_dose, max_dose can be changed freely between calls.

    Output:

  • None: model's objective, quadratic constraint QCRHS values, and variable bounds are updated in place. Call model.optimize() afterwards as usual.

class MOO(abc.ABC): 
110class MOO(ABC):
111    _valid_parameter_names = [
112        "dose_voxel_goal",
113        "penalty_weight_linear",
114        "penalty_weight_quadratic",
115        "penalty_weight_hotspot",
116        "hotspot_threshold",
117        "penalty_weight_uniformity",
118        "penalty_weight_variance_time",
119    ]
120
121    @abstractmethod
122    def __init__(
123        self,
124        catheter_table_optim: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi,
125        parameter_space: Dict[str, np.typing.ArrayLike],
126        max_workers: int = 16,
127        normalize: bool = False,
128        anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] = None,
129        slack_space_shrinkage: float = None,
130        slack_objective_threshold: float | Dict[str, float] = 0,
131    ):
132        r"""
133        ### Purpose:
134        - The multi-objective optimization class performs hyper-parameter tuning
135        to yield clinically acceptable treatment plans with Pareto optimal DVHs.
136        The definition of clinically acceptale is set by the dvh metric goals inside
137        the BrachyPlan of the `catheter_table_optim`.
138
139        ### Inputs:
140        - `catheter_table_optim` := An optimization object with a BrachyPlan and
141        a Gurobi model. The plan shold have DVH metrics goal loaded.
142        - `parameter_space` := A dictionary mapping the names of the parameters to be
143        optimized to their range [min, max]. The names of the parameters are
144        some attributes of the Optimization_Config class followed by the name of
145        that structure in paranthesis. For example:
146            penalty_weight_linear(CTV) : [1, 500]
147        - `normalize` := If true dvh_metric_goals would be normalized from 100% to 1.
148        Be sure that the DVH metrics are in percentage form (defualt is percentage).
149        - `anchor_dvh_metric`: Dict[str, float] := Provide a DVH metric name to be used for
150        anchoring the plan, i.e. the dwell times will be scaled so that the desired value for
151        this metric is met. Example: {"V100%(CTV)": 95} will scale the dwell times so that V100%(CTV) = 95.
152        - `slack_space_shrinkage`: float := Based on random sampling, the parameter space
153        is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans. 
154        This value is slack on relaxing the DVH metric goals. For example, if the DVH metric 
155        goal is [">=", 100] and the slack is 0.1, then the parameter space will be shrunk to
156        focus on the region of parameters that yield plans with DVH metric >= 90.
157        
158        ### Outputs:
159        None := Fills out the following attributes:
160        - `self.dvh_metric_goals` := maps the DVH names {metric_name
161        (structure_name)} to their clinically desired values. Metrics with a `None` goal 
162        (i.e. not clinically constrained/tracked) are skipped entirely and never appear here.
163        - `self.trial_data`: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing 
164        the result of all the trials. The columns are parameter names from
165        the keys of `self.parameter_space` and the dvh metric names from the keys of `self.dvh_metric_goals`.
166        - `self.directions`: Dict[str, str] := A dictionary of directions for each DVH 
167        metric goal. The order of the directions corresponds to the order of 
168        the keys in `self.dvh_metric_goals`. The direction is either "minimize" 
169        or "maximize" depending on the operation in the dvh_metric_goals. For example,
170        if the operation is "<=", then the direction is "minimize". If the operation is ">=", 
171        then the direction is "maximize".
172        - `self.tuner`: Any := The tuner object that will be used to recommend the next 
173        batch of parameter queries to be evaluated.
174        - `self.max_workers`: int := The maximum number of workers to use for parallel evaluation.
175        - `self.normalize`: bool := If true dvh_metric_goals would be normalized from 100% to 1.
176        This is lowkey trash, don't use it.
177        - `self.anchor_dvh_metric`: Dict[str, float] := Provide a DVH metric name to be used for
178        anchoring the plan, i.e. the dwell times will be scaled so that the desired
179        value for this metric is met. Example: {"V100%(CTV)": 95} will scale the dwell times so 
180        that V100%(CTV) = 95.
181        - `self.slack_space_shrinkage`: float := Based on random sampling, the parameter space
182        is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans
183        with some slack.
184        - `slack_objective_threshold`: Relative slack for each DVH outcome
185        constraint. A float applies to all metrics; a dictionary sets slack
186        by DVH metric name (unspecified metrics use zero slack). Values must
187        be in [-1, 1]. Positive slack relaxes constraints and negative slack
188        tightens them. For a goal of `">= 100"`, slack `0.1` sets the Ax
189        constraint to `>= 90`; for a goal of `"<= 100"`, it sets it to
190        `<= 110`.
191
192        The object has the following abstract methods that must be implemented in a subclass:
193        - `set_tuner()` := Builds the Tuner object that will recommend the next batch
194        of parameter queries to be evaluated.
195        - `run_random_sampling(n_samples: int, use_for_warmup: bool = True)` := To run random
196        sampling for `n_samples` of the parameter space.
197        - `run_trials(n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1)` := To run the multi-objective optimization
198        for `n_trials` outer iterations.
199        """
200        self.catheter_table_optim = catheter_table_optim
201        self.parameter_space = parameter_space
202        self.max_workers = max_workers
203        self.normalize = normalize
204        self.anchor_dvh_metric = anchor_dvh_metric
205        self.slack_space_shrinkage = slack_space_shrinkage
206        # # Attributes to be filled out
207        self.dvh_metric_goals: Dict[str, List] = None
208        self.tuner: Any = None
209        self.trial_data: pd.DataFrame = None
210        self.directions = None
211        # # Fill out the attributes
212        self._validate_init()
213        self._set_directions_from_dvh_metric_goals()
214        self._set_slack_objective_threshold(slack_objective_threshold)
215
216    def _validate_init(self):
217        r"""
218        ### Purpose:
219        - To ensure `self.catheter_table_optim` and `parameter_space` contain
220        the correct information.
221
222        ### Inputs:
223        None := Expects the following to be filled already:
224        - `self.catheter_table_optim`
225        - `self.parameter_space`
226
227        ### Outputs:
228        None := Fills out the following attributes:
229        - `self.dvh_metric_goals` := maps the DVH names {metric_name(structure_name)}
230        to their clinically desired values. Metrics with a `None` goal (i.e. not
231        clinically constrained/tracked) are skipped entirely and never appear here.
232        - `self.trial_data`: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing the result of
233        all the trials. The columns are parameter names from the keys of
234        `self.parameter_space` and the dvh metric names from the keys of
235        `self.dvh_metric_goals`.
236        """
237        self.dvh_metric_goals = {}
238        for value in self.catheter_table_optim.plan.dvh_metric_goals.values():
239            for dvh in value["dvh_metric_goals"]:
240                if value["dvh_metric_goals"].get(dvh, None) is not None:
241                    self.dvh_metric_goals[dvh] = value["dvh_metric_goals"][dvh]
242                    if self.normalize:
243                        self.dvh_metric_goals[dvh] = [
244                            self.dvh_metric_goals[dvh][0],
245                            self.dvh_metric_goals[dvh][1]/100,
246                        ]
247
248        if (
249            self.dvh_metric_goals is None
250            or len(self.dvh_metric_goals) == 0
251            or isinstance(self.dvh_metric_goals, list)):
252            raise ValueError("The DVH metric goal dictionary is essential for \
253multi-objective optimization. please provide it to the optimization object.")
254
255        for key, value in self.dvh_metric_goals.items():
256            wrong_value = False
257            if not isinstance(value, list):
258                wrong_value = True
259            elif len(value) != 2:
260                wrong_value = True
261            elif value[0] not in ["<=", ">="]:
262                wrong_value = True
263            elif not isinstance(value[1], (int, float)):
264                wrong_value = True
265            if wrong_value:
266                raise ValueError(f"The value of the DVH metric goal: {key} \
267should be a list of string operation (one of ['<=', '>=']) and float \
268see `BrachyStructure.set_dvh_metric_goals()` for more details.")
269
270        for key in self.parameter_space.keys():
271            structure_name = key.split("(")[-1].split(")")[0]
272            parameter_name = key.split("(")[0]
273
274            structure_found = False
275            parameter_found = False
276            for optim_config in self.catheter_table_optim.plan.optimization_config_dict.values():
277                if optim_config.structure_name == structure_name:
278                    structure_found = True
279                if parameter_name in MOO._valid_parameter_names:
280                    parameter_found = True
281
282            if not structure_found:
283                raise ValueError(f"The structure: {structure_name} was not found in the \
284optimization config dict of the plan")
285            if not parameter_found:
286                raise ValueError(f"The parameter: {parameter_name} was not found in the \
287as a valid optimization parameter. Please see `Optimization_Config.to_dict()`")
288
289        # # Now build the columns of the master trial dataframe
290        self.trial_data = pd.DataFrame(
291            columns=(
292                list(self.parameter_space.keys())
293                + list(self.dvh_metric_goals.keys())
294                + ["sampler_name_id", "acceptable", "hypervolume"]))
295
296    def _set_slack_objective_threshold(self, slack_objective_threshold):
297        if isinstance(slack_objective_threshold, dict):
298            for key, value in slack_objective_threshold.items():
299                if value < -1 or value > 1:
300                    raise ValueError(f"slack factor for {key} should be between -1 and 1")
301        else:
302            if (slack_objective_threshold < -1
303                or slack_objective_threshold > 1):
304                raise ValueError("slack factor should be between -1 and 1")
305            slack_objective_threshold_dict = {}
306            for dvh_name in self.dvh_metric_goals.keys():
307                slack_objective_threshold_dict[dvh_name] = slack_objective_threshold
308            self.slack_objective_threshold = slack_objective_threshold_dict
309
310
311    def objectives(
312        self,
313        parameters:pd.DataFrame,
314        sampler_name_id: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
315        r"""
316        ### Purpose:
317        - To evaluate the objectives for the parameters generated in each trial.
318        The objectives are the DVH metrics in the order set by the keys in self.dvh_metric_goals.
319        - All parameters passed here are evaluated together in a single, batched call to
320        `evaluate_parameters()`, which parallelizes the underlying Gurobi solves across
321        `self.max_workers` threads.
322        - Also calculates the hyper-volume and whetheter each parameter lead to acceptable
323        dvh metrics or not.
324        - Lastly, `self.trial_data` is updated with all the information:
325            - parameter values
326            - dvh metrics observed
327            - hyper volume
328            - acceptability
329
330        ### Inputs:
331        - parameters := A dataframe of parameters to be evaluated. The columns are the names
332        of the parameters while the rows are parameter values for each trial.
333        - sampler_name_id: str := The name of the sampler being used. This is used to
334        keep track of which sampler was used for each trial in the `self.trial_data` dataframe.
335
336        ### Outputs:
337        - A dataframe with the dvh metrics specified by the keys in self.dvh_metric_goals.
338        """
339        dvh_metrics_data = evaluate_parameters(
340            parameters,
341            self.catheter_table_optim,
342            max_workers=self.max_workers,
343            anchor_dvh_metric=self.anchor_dvh_metric,
344        )
345        acceptable_trials = are_acceptable(dvh_metrics_data, self.dvh_metric_goals)
346        hv_trials = get_hyper_volume(dvh_metrics_data, self.dvh_metric_goals)
347        sampler_df = pd.Series(
348            [sampler_name_id for _ in range(len(parameters))],
349            name="sampler_name_id").to_frame()
350        self.trial_data = pd.concat([
351            self.trial_data,
352            pd.concat([
353                parameters.reset_index(drop=True), dvh_metrics_data,
354                acceptable_trials, hv_trials, sampler_df], axis=1)
355        ], axis=0)
356        self.trial_data.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)
357
358        return dvh_metrics_data[list(self.dvh_metric_goals.keys())]

369    @abstractmethod
370    def run_random_sampling(
371        self,
372        n_samples: int,
373        use_for_warmup: bool = True
374    ):
375        r"""
376        ### Purpose:
377        - To run random sampling for `n_samples`. of the parameter space
378        evaluated either sequentially or in parallel.
379
380        ### Inputs:
381        - n_samples: int := The number of samples to generate and evaluate.
382        - use_for_warmup: bool := If True, the random samples will be used to warm up
383        the tuner. If False, the random samples will just be stored to self.trial_data.
384
385        ### Outputs:
386        None := Fills out the following attributes:
387        - `self.trial_data`: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing the result of
388        all the trials. The columns are parameter names from the keys of
389        `self.parameter_space` and the dvh metric names from the keys of
390        `self.dvh_metric_goals`.
391        """
392        pass
393
394    @abstractmethod
395    def run_trials(self, n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1):
396        r"""
397        ### Purpose:
398        - To run the multi-objective optimization for `n_trials` outer iterations.
399        On each iteration, `batch_size` trials are asked for at once and evaluated
400        together in a single batched call to `objectives()` (which itself parallelizes
401        the Gurobi solves via `self.max_workers`), then each trial is told back to the
402        study individually. The total number of trials evaluated across the whole run
403        is `n_trials * batch_size`.
404        - When `batch_size == 1` this reduces to the original sequential ask/evaluate/tell
405        loop.
406
407        ### Inputs:
408        - n_trials: int := The number of outer iterations (batches) to run.
409        - batch_size: int := The number of trials to ask for and evaluate together on
410        each iteration. Total trials evaluated = n_trials * batch_size.
411
412        ### Outputs:
413        None := Fills out the following attributes:
414        - `self.trial_data`: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing the result of
415        all the trials. The columns are parameter names from the keys of
416        `self.parameter_space` and the dvh metric names from the keys of
417        `self.dvh_metric_goals`.
418        """
419        pass
420
421    def _set_directions_from_dvh_metric_goals(self):
422        r"""
423        ### Purpose:
424        - To get the directions of optimization for each DVH metric goal.
425        The direction is either "minimize" or "maximize" depending on the
426        operation in the dvh_metric_goals. For example, if the operation is "<=",
427        then the direction is "minimize". If the operation is ">=", then the direction
428        is "maximize".
429        ### Inputs:
430        None := Expects self.dvh_metric_goals to be filled out.
431
432        ### Outputs:
433        -None:= sets self.directions: Dict[str, str] := A dictionary of directions for each DVH metric goal.
434        The order of the directions corresponds to the order of the keys in
435        self.dvh_metric_goals.
436        """
437        directions = {}
438        for key, value in self.dvh_metric_goals.items():
439            if value[0] == "<=":
440                directions[key] = "minimize"
441            elif value[0] == ">=":
442                directions[key] = "maximize"
443            else:
444                raise ValueError(f"The operation: {value[0]} \
445for DVH metric goal: {key} is not valid. Please use one of ['<=', '>=']")
446        self.directions = directions
447

480    def shrink_parameter_space(self, return_acceptable_trials: bool = False):
481        r"""
482        ### Purpose:
483        - To shrink the parameter space based on the observed dvh metrics and the dvh metric goals.
484        The parameter space is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically
485        acceptable plans. This is done by relaxing the dvh metric goals by a fraction of
486        `self.slack_space_shrinkage` and then finding the range of parameters that yield
487        plans that meet the relaxed goals.
488
489        - Be sure to update the parameter space in the self.tuner afterwards
490
491        ### Inputs:
492        - return_acceptable_trials: bool := If True, returns a dataframe with the trials that meet the relaxed goals.
493        - Expects self.trial_data to be filled out with at least one trial.
494
495        ### Outputs:
496        None := Updates self.parameter_space with the new shrunk parameter space.
497        - If return_acceptable_trials is True, returns a dataframe with the trials that meet the relaxed goals.
498        """
499        if self.slack_space_shrinkage is None:
500            return
501        if self.slack_space_shrinkage <= -1 or self.slack_space_shrinkage >= 1:
502            raise ValueError("slack_space_shrinkage should be between -1 and 1.")
503        if len(self.trial_data) == 0:
504            raise ValueError("No trials have been run yet. Cannot shrink parameter space.")
505
506        # # Relax the dvh metric goals by a fraction of slack_space_shrinkage
507        relaxed_dvh_metric_goals = {}
508        for key, value in self.dvh_metric_goals.items():
509            if value[0] == "<=":
510                relaxed_dvh_metric_goals[key] = [
511                    value[0],
512                    value[1] * (1 + self.slack_space_shrinkage),
513                ]
514            elif value[0] == ">=":
515                relaxed_dvh_metric_goals[key] = [
516                    value[0],
517                    value[1] * (1 - self.slack_space_shrinkage),
518                ]
519            else:
520                raise ValueError(f"The operation: {value[0]} \
521for DVH metric goal: {key} is not valid. Please use one of ['<=', '>=']")
522
523        # # Find the min and max of the parameters that yield plans that meet the relaxed goals
524        acceptable_trials = are_acceptable(
525            self.trial_data[list(self.dvh_metric_goals.keys())],
526            relaxed_dvh_metric_goals)
527        for param in self.parameter_space.keys():
528            param_values = self.trial_data.loc[acceptable_trials["acceptable"], param]
529            if len(param_values) == 0:
530                raise ValueError("No acceptable trials found. Cannot shrink parameter space.")
531            self.parameter_space[param] = [param_values.min(), param_values.max()]
532        if return_acceptable_trials:
533            return acceptable_trials

Helper class that provides a standard way to create an ABC using inheritance.

@abstractmethod
MOO( catheter_table_optim: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi, parameter_space: Dict[str, Union[Buffer, numpy._typing._array_like._SupportsArray[numpy.dtype[Any]], numpy._typing._nested_sequence._NestedSequence[numpy._typing._array_like._SupportsArray[numpy.dtype[Any]]], bool, int, float, complex, str, bytes, numpy._typing._nested_sequence._NestedSequence[bool | int | float | complex | str | bytes]]], max_workers: int = 16, normalize: bool = False, anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] = None, slack_space_shrinkage: float = None, slack_objective_threshold: Union[float, Dict[str, float]] = 0) 
121    @abstractmethod
122    def __init__(
123        self,
124        catheter_table_optim: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi,
125        parameter_space: Dict[str, np.typing.ArrayLike],
126        max_workers: int = 16,
127        normalize: bool = False,
128        anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] = None,
129        slack_space_shrinkage: float = None,
130        slack_objective_threshold: float | Dict[str, float] = 0,
131    ):
132        r"""
133        ### Purpose:
134        - The multi-objective optimization class performs hyper-parameter tuning
135        to yield clinically acceptable treatment plans with Pareto optimal DVHs.
136        The definition of clinically acceptale is set by the dvh metric goals inside
137        the BrachyPlan of the `catheter_table_optim`.
138
139        ### Inputs:
140        - `catheter_table_optim` := An optimization object with a BrachyPlan and
141        a Gurobi model. The plan shold have DVH metrics goal loaded.
142        - `parameter_space` := A dictionary mapping the names of the parameters to be
143        optimized to their range [min, max]. The names of the parameters are
144        some attributes of the Optimization_Config class followed by the name of
145        that structure in paranthesis. For example:
146            penalty_weight_linear(CTV) : [1, 500]
147        - `normalize` := If true dvh_metric_goals would be normalized from 100% to 1.
148        Be sure that the DVH metrics are in percentage form (defualt is percentage).
149        - `anchor_dvh_metric`: Dict[str, float] := Provide a DVH metric name to be used for
150        anchoring the plan, i.e. the dwell times will be scaled so that the desired value for
151        this metric is met. Example: {"V100%(CTV)": 95} will scale the dwell times so that V100%(CTV) = 95.
152        - `slack_space_shrinkage`: float := Based on random sampling, the parameter space
153        is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans. 
154        This value is slack on relaxing the DVH metric goals. For example, if the DVH metric 
155        goal is [">=", 100] and the slack is 0.1, then the parameter space will be shrunk to
156        focus on the region of parameters that yield plans with DVH metric >= 90.
157        
158        ### Outputs:
159        None := Fills out the following attributes:
160        - `self.dvh_metric_goals` := maps the DVH names {metric_name
161        (structure_name)} to their clinically desired values. Metrics with a `None` goal 
162        (i.e. not clinically constrained/tracked) are skipped entirely and never appear here.
163        - `self.trial_data`: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing 
164        the result of all the trials. The columns are parameter names from
165        the keys of `self.parameter_space` and the dvh metric names from the keys of `self.dvh_metric_goals`.
166        - `self.directions`: Dict[str, str] := A dictionary of directions for each DVH 
167        metric goal. The order of the directions corresponds to the order of 
168        the keys in `self.dvh_metric_goals`. The direction is either "minimize" 
169        or "maximize" depending on the operation in the dvh_metric_goals. For example,
170        if the operation is "<=", then the direction is "minimize". If the operation is ">=", 
171        then the direction is "maximize".
172        - `self.tuner`: Any := The tuner object that will be used to recommend the next 
173        batch of parameter queries to be evaluated.
174        - `self.max_workers`: int := The maximum number of workers to use for parallel evaluation.
175        - `self.normalize`: bool := If true dvh_metric_goals would be normalized from 100% to 1.
176        This is lowkey trash, don't use it.
177        - `self.anchor_dvh_metric`: Dict[str, float] := Provide a DVH metric name to be used for
178        anchoring the plan, i.e. the dwell times will be scaled so that the desired
179        value for this metric is met. Example: {"V100%(CTV)": 95} will scale the dwell times so 
180        that V100%(CTV) = 95.
181        - `self.slack_space_shrinkage`: float := Based on random sampling, the parameter space
182        is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans
183        with some slack.
184        - `slack_objective_threshold`: Relative slack for each DVH outcome
185        constraint. A float applies to all metrics; a dictionary sets slack
186        by DVH metric name (unspecified metrics use zero slack). Values must
187        be in [-1, 1]. Positive slack relaxes constraints and negative slack
188        tightens them. For a goal of `">= 100"`, slack `0.1` sets the Ax
189        constraint to `>= 90`; for a goal of `"<= 100"`, it sets it to
190        `<= 110`.
191
192        The object has the following abstract methods that must be implemented in a subclass:
193        - `set_tuner()` := Builds the Tuner object that will recommend the next batch
194        of parameter queries to be evaluated.
195        - `run_random_sampling(n_samples: int, use_for_warmup: bool = True)` := To run random
196        sampling for `n_samples` of the parameter space.
197        - `run_trials(n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1)` := To run the multi-objective optimization
198        for `n_trials` outer iterations.
199        """
200        self.catheter_table_optim = catheter_table_optim
201        self.parameter_space = parameter_space
202        self.max_workers = max_workers
203        self.normalize = normalize
204        self.anchor_dvh_metric = anchor_dvh_metric
205        self.slack_space_shrinkage = slack_space_shrinkage
206        # # Attributes to be filled out
207        self.dvh_metric_goals: Dict[str, List] = None
208        self.tuner: Any = None
209        self.trial_data: pd.DataFrame = None
210        self.directions = None
211        # # Fill out the attributes
212        self._validate_init()
213        self._set_directions_from_dvh_metric_goals()
214        self._set_slack_objective_threshold(slack_objective_threshold)

Purpose:

  • The multi-objective optimization class performs hyper-parameter tuning to yield clinically acceptable treatment plans with Pareto optimal DVHs. The definition of clinically acceptale is set by the dvh metric goals inside the BrachyPlan of the catheter_table_optim.

Inputs:

  • catheter_table_optim := An optimization object with a BrachyPlan and a Gurobi model. The plan shold have DVH metrics goal loaded.
  • parameter_space := A dictionary mapping the names of the parameters to be optimized to their range [min, max]. The names of the parameters are some attributes of the Optimization_Config class followed by the name of that structure in paranthesis. For example: penalty_weight_linear(CTV) : [1, 500]
  • normalize := If true dvh_metric_goals would be normalized from 100% to 1. Be sure that the DVH metrics are in percentage form (defualt is percentage).
  • anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] := Provide a DVH metric name to be used for anchoring the plan, i.e. the dwell times will be scaled so that the desired value for this metric is met. Example: {"V100%(CTV)": 95} will scale the dwell times so that V100%(CTV) = 95.
  • slack_space_shrinkage: float := Based on random sampling, the parameter space is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans. This value is slack on relaxing the DVH metric goals. For example, if the DVH metric goal is [">=", 100] and the slack is 0.1, then the parameter space will be shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield plans with DVH metric >= 90.

Outputs:

None := Fills out the following attributes:

  • self.dvh_metric_goals := maps the DVH names {metric_name (structure_name)} to their clinically desired values. Metrics with a None goal (i.e. not clinically constrained/tracked) are skipped entirely and never appear here.
  • self.trial_data: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing the result of all the trials. The columns are parameter names from the keys of self.parameter_space and the dvh metric names from the keys of self.dvh_metric_goals.
  • self.directions: Dict[str, str] := A dictionary of directions for each DVH metric goal. The order of the directions corresponds to the order of the keys in self.dvh_metric_goals. The direction is either "minimize" or "maximize" depending on the operation in the dvh_metric_goals. For example, if the operation is "<=", then the direction is "minimize". If the operation is ">=", then the direction is "maximize".
  • self.tuner: Any := The tuner object that will be used to recommend the next batch of parameter queries to be evaluated.
  • self.max_workers: int := The maximum number of workers to use for parallel evaluation.
  • self.normalize: bool := If true dvh_metric_goals would be normalized from 100% to 1. This is lowkey trash, don't use it.
  • self.anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] := Provide a DVH metric name to be used for anchoring the plan, i.e. the dwell times will be scaled so that the desired value for this metric is met. Example: {"V100%(CTV)": 95} will scale the dwell times so that V100%(CTV) = 95.
  • self.slack_space_shrinkage: float := Based on random sampling, the parameter space is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans with some slack.
  • slack_objective_threshold: Relative slack for each DVH outcome constraint. A float applies to all metrics; a dictionary sets slack by DVH metric name (unspecified metrics use zero slack). Values must be in [-1, 1]. Positive slack relaxes constraints and negative slack tightens them. For a goal of ">= 100", slack 0.1 sets the Ax constraint to >= 90; for a goal of "<= 100", it sets it to <= 110.

The object has the following abstract methods that must be implemented in a subclass:

  • set_tuner() := Builds the Tuner object that will recommend the next batch of parameter queries to be evaluated.
  • run_random_sampling(n_samples: int, use_for_warmup: bool = True) := To run random sampling for n_samples of the parameter space.
  • run_trials(n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1) := To run the multi-objective optimization for n_trials outer iterations.

@abstractmethod
def run_trials(self, n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1): 
394    @abstractmethod
395    def run_trials(self, n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1):
396        r"""
397        ### Purpose:
398        - To run the multi-objective optimization for `n_trials` outer iterations.
399        On each iteration, `batch_size` trials are asked for at once and evaluated
400        together in a single batched call to `objectives()` (which itself parallelizes
401        the Gurobi solves via `self.max_workers`), then each trial is told back to the
402        study individually. The total number of trials evaluated across the whole run
403        is `n_trials * batch_size`.
404        - When `batch_size == 1` this reduces to the original sequential ask/evaluate/tell
405        loop.
406
407        ### Inputs:
408        - n_trials: int := The number of outer iterations (batches) to run.
409        - batch_size: int := The number of trials to ask for and evaluate together on
410        each iteration. Total trials evaluated = n_trials * batch_size.
411
412        ### Outputs:
413        None := Fills out the following attributes:
414        - `self.trial_data`: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing the result of
415        all the trials. The columns are parameter names from the keys of
416        `self.parameter_space` and the dvh metric names from the keys of
417        `self.dvh_metric_goals`.
418        """
419        pass

The total number of trials evaluated across the whole run is n_trials * batch_size.
  • When batch_size == 1 this reduces to the original sequential ask/evaluate/tell loop.

def shrink_parameter_space(self, return_acceptable_trials: bool = False): 
480    def shrink_parameter_space(self, return_acceptable_trials: bool = False):
481        r"""
482        ### Purpose:
483        - To shrink the parameter space based on the observed dvh metrics and the dvh metric goals.
484        The parameter space is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically
485        acceptable plans. This is done by relaxing the dvh metric goals by a fraction of
486        `self.slack_space_shrinkage` and then finding the range of parameters that yield
487        plans that meet the relaxed goals.
488
489        - Be sure to update the parameter space in the self.tuner afterwards
490
491        ### Inputs:
492        - return_acceptable_trials: bool := If True, returns a dataframe with the trials that meet the relaxed goals.
493        - Expects self.trial_data to be filled out with at least one trial.
494
495        ### Outputs:
496        None := Updates self.parameter_space with the new shrunk parameter space.
497        - If return_acceptable_trials is True, returns a dataframe with the trials that meet the relaxed goals.
498        """
499        if self.slack_space_shrinkage is None:
500            return
501        if self.slack_space_shrinkage <= -1 or self.slack_space_shrinkage >= 1:
502            raise ValueError("slack_space_shrinkage should be between -1 and 1.")
503        if len(self.trial_data) == 0:
504            raise ValueError("No trials have been run yet. Cannot shrink parameter space.")
505
506        # # Relax the dvh metric goals by a fraction of slack_space_shrinkage
507        relaxed_dvh_metric_goals = {}
508        for key, value in self.dvh_metric_goals.items():
509            if value[0] == "<=":
510                relaxed_dvh_metric_goals[key] = [
511                    value[0],
512                    value[1] * (1 + self.slack_space_shrinkage),
513                ]
514            elif value[0] == ">=":
515                relaxed_dvh_metric_goals[key] = [
516                    value[0],
517                    value[1] * (1 - self.slack_space_shrinkage),
518                ]
519            else:
520                raise ValueError(f"The operation: {value[0]} \
521for DVH metric goal: {key} is not valid. Please use one of ['<=', '>=']")
522
523        # # Find the min and max of the parameters that yield plans that meet the relaxed goals
524        acceptable_trials = are_acceptable(
525            self.trial_data[list(self.dvh_metric_goals.keys())],
526            relaxed_dvh_metric_goals)
527        for param in self.parameter_space.keys():
528            param_values = self.trial_data.loc[acceptable_trials["acceptable"], param]
529            if len(param_values) == 0:
530                raise ValueError("No acceptable trials found. Cannot shrink parameter space.")
531            self.parameter_space[param] = [param_values.min(), param_values.max()]
532        if return_acceptable_trials:
533            return acceptable_trials

Purpose:

  • To shrink the parameter space based on the observed dvh metrics and the dvh metric goals. The parameter space is shrunk to focus on the region of parameters that yield clinically acceptable plans. This is done by relaxing the dvh metric goals by a fraction of self.slack_space_shrinkage and then finding the range of parameters that yield plans that meet the relaxed goals.

  • Be sure to update the parameter space in the self.tuner afterwards

Inputs:

  • return_acceptable_trials: bool := If True, returns a dataframe with the trials that meet the relaxed goals.
  • Expects self.trial_data to be filled out with at least one trial.

Outputs:

None := Updates self.parameter_space with the new shrunk parameter space.

  • If return_acceptable_trials is True, returns a dataframe with the trials that meet the relaxed goals.
def evaluate_parameters( parameters: pandas.core.frame.DataFrame, optim_obj: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi, max_workers: int = 16, normalize: bool = False, anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] = None) -> pandas.core.frame.DataFrame: 
 34def evaluate_parameters(
 35    parameters: pd.DataFrame,
 36    optim_obj: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi,
 37    max_workers: int = 16,
 38    normalize: bool = False,
 39    anchor_dvh_metric: Dict[str, float] = None
 40) -> pd.DataFrame:
 41    r"""
 42    ### Purpose:
 43    - Evaluates the parameters (i.e. penalty weights and target dose) and
 44    returns the observed dvh metrics corresponding to those parameters.
 45
 46    ### Inputs:
 47    - `parameters`: pd.DataFrame := A dataframe with the parameters to be evaluated.
 48    The columns are the parameter names and the rows are the different parameter sets to be evaluated.
 49    - `optim_obj`: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi := The optimization object that will be used to evaluate the parameters.
 50    - `max_workers`: int := The maximum number of workers to use for parallel evaluation.
 51    If max_workers is 1, the evaluation will be done sequentially.
 52    - `normalize`: If True, the dvh metric values are devided by 100.
 53    - `anchor_dvh_metric` := The dwell times are scaled to match the desired value for 
 54    the dvh metric provided. Only one anchor can be provided in the format of {dvh_metric_name: value}
 55    ### Outputs:
 56    - `dvh_metrics_data`: pd.DataFrame := A dataframe with the observed dvh metrics
 57    corresponding to the evaluated parameters. The columns are the dvh metric names and
 58    the rows are the different parameter sets that were evaluated.
 59    """
 60    model_list = []
 61    optimization_configs = list(optim_obj.plan.optimization_config_dict.values())
 62    for row in range(parameters.shape[0]):
 63        model = optim_obj.model.copy()
 64        _update_optimization_configs_with_parameters(
 65            parameters.iloc[row:row + 1],
 66            optimization_configs)
 67        update_penalty_weights_and_voxel_goals(
 68            model,
 69            optimization_configs)
 70        model_list.append(model)
 71
 72    if max_workers > 1:
 73        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
 74            futures = [
 75                executor.submit(get_optimized_dwelltimes_from_model, model)
 76                for model in model_list]
 77            dvh_metrics_list = []
 78            for future in as_completed(futures):
 79                dwell_time_dict = future.result()[0]
 80                optim_obj.plan.catheter_table.set_dwelltimes_by_names(
 81                    dwell_time_dict)
 82                dvh_metrics = optim_obj.plan.get_dvh_metrics()
 83                if anchor_dvh_metric is not None:
 84                    dvh_metrics = _anchor_plan_to_dvh_metric(
 85                        plan=optim_obj.plan,
 86                        anchor_dvh_metric=anchor_dvh_metric,
 87                        observed_dvh_metrics=dvh_metrics,)
 88                if normalize:
 89                    for key in dvh_metrics:
 90                        dvh_metrics[key] = dvh_metrics[key]/100
 91                dvh_metrics_list.append(dvh_metrics)
 92    else:
 93        dvh_metrics_list = []
 94        for model in model_list:
 95            dwell_time_dict = get_optimized_dwelltimes_from_model(model)[0]
 96            optim_obj.plan.catheter_table.set_dwelltimes_by_names(
 97                dwell_time_dict)
 98            dvh_metrics = optim_obj.plan.get_dvh_metrics()
 99            if anchor_dvh_metric is not None:
100                dvh_metrics = _anchor_plan_to_dvh_metric(
101                    plan=optim_obj.plan,
102                    anchor_dvh_metric=anchor_dvh_metric,
103                    observed_dvh_metrics=dvh_metrics,)
104            if normalize:
105                for key in dvh_metrics:
106                    dvh_metrics[key] = dvh_metrics[key]/100
107            dvh_metrics_list.append(dvh_metrics)        
108    return pd.DataFrame(dvh_metrics_list)

Purpose:

  • Evaluates the parameters (i.e. penalty weights and target dose) and returns the observed dvh metrics corresponding to those parameters.

Inputs:

  • parameters: pd.DataFrame := A dataframe with the parameters to be evaluated. The columns are the parameter names and the rows are the different parameter sets to be evaluated.
  • optim_obj: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi := The optimization object that will be used to evaluate the parameters.
  • max_workers: int := The maximum number of workers to use for parallel evaluation. If max_workers is 1, the evaluation will be done sequentially.
  • normalize: If True, the dvh metric values are devided by 100.

  • anchor_dvh_metric := The dwell times are scaled to match the desired value for the dvh metric provided. Only one anchor can be provided in the format of {dvh_metric_name: value}

    Outputs:

  • dvh_metrics_data: pd.DataFrame := A dataframe with the observed dvh metrics corresponding to the evaluated parameters. The columns are the dvh metric names and the rows are the different parameter sets that were evaluated.

def are_acceptable( dvh_metrics: pandas.core.frame.DataFrame, dvh_metric_goals: Dict) -> pandas.core.frame.DataFrame: 
535def are_acceptable(
536    dvh_metrics: pd.DataFrame,
537    dvh_metric_goals: Dict
538    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
539    r"""
540    ### Purpose:
541    - To assess if the provided dvh metrics are acceptable according to
542    the dvh metric goals
543
544    ### Inputs:
545    - dvh_metrics := DVH metric names and their observed values
546    - dvh_metric_goals := The operation and goal for each DVH metrics
547    Ex. D95%(CTV): [">=", 100]    
548    
549    ### Outputs:
550    - results_df: pd.DataFrame := a data frame containing boolean values
551    for each row of the dvh_metrics. 
552    """
553    results_df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["acceptable"])
554    for i, row in dvh_metrics.iterrows():    
555        acceptable = True
556        for key, value in dvh_metric_goals.items():
557            observed_value = row.get(key, None)
558            if observed_value is None:
559                acceptable = False
560            else:
561                if value[0] == "<=":
562                    if not observed_value <= value[1]:
563                        acceptable = False
564                        break
565                if value[0] == ">=":
566                    if not observed_value >= value[1]:
567                        acceptable = False
568                        break
569        results_df.loc[i] = acceptable
570    return results_df

Purpose:

  • To assess if the provided dvh metrics are acceptable according to the dvh metric goals

Inputs:

  • dvh_metrics := DVH metric names and their observed values
  • dvh_metric_goals := The operation and goal for each DVH metrics Ex. D95%(CTV): [">=", 100]

Outputs:

  • results_df: pd.DataFrame := a data frame containing boolean values for each row of the dvh_metrics.
def get_hyper_volume( dvh_metrics: pandas.core.frame.DataFrame, dvh_metric_goals: dict[str, list], return_series: bool = True): 
572def get_hyper_volume(
573    dvh_metrics: pd.DataFrame, 
574    dvh_metric_goals: dict[str, list],
575    return_series: bool = True
576):
577    """
578    ### Purpose:
579    - Computes hypervolume for valid points and a negative penalty score
580    for points violating at least one DVH requirement.
581
582    ### Inputs
583        - dvh_metrics: pd.DataFrame with candidate solutions as rows.
584        - dvh_metric_goals: dict mapping metric -> [operator ('>=' or '<='), threshold].
585        - return_series: If True, returns a pd.Series with scores for each individual row.
586        If False, returns a single float (joint HV of valid set, 
587        or worst negative violation if no point is valid).
588    """
589    ordered_keys = list(dvh_metric_goals.keys())
590    
591    # 1. Parse operators and reference points
592    signs = []
593    ref_values = []
594    raw_thresholds = []
595    for key in ordered_keys:
596        op, threshold = dvh_metric_goals[key]
597        raw_thresholds.append(float(threshold))
598        if op == ">=":
599            signs.append(1.0)
600            ref_values.append(float(threshold))
601        elif op == "<=":
602            signs.append(-1.0)
603            ref_values.append(-float(threshold))
604        else:
605            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported operation '{op}' for '{key}'.")
606
607    sign_tensor = torch.tensor(signs, dtype=torch.double)
608    ref_point = torch.tensor(ref_values, dtype=torch.double)
609    scale = torch.tensor([max(abs(t), 1.0) for t in raw_thresholds], dtype=torch.double)
610
611    # 2. Align to BoTorch maximization format (Y >= ref_point is feasible)
612    metric_matrix = dvh_metrics[ordered_keys].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
613    Y = torch.tensor(metric_matrix, dtype=torch.double) * sign_tensor
614
615    # 3. Evaluate each solution row-by-row
616    hv_calculator = Hypervolume(ref_point=ref_point)
617    scores = []
618
619    for i in range(Y.shape[0]):
620        y_i = Y[i]
621        diff = y_i - ref_point  # diff >= 0 means goal is satisfied
622        
623        if (diff >= 0).all():
624            # Solution meets all goals: compute positive individual hypervolume
625            val = float(hv_calculator.compute(y_i.unsqueeze(0)))
626            scores.append(val)
627        else:
628            # Solution violates at least one goal: compute negative relative violation
629            violations = torch.clamp(-diff, min=0.0)
630            rel_violation = (violations / scale).sum().item()
631            scores.append(-rel_violation)
632
633    score_series = pd.Series(scores, index=dvh_metrics.index, name="hypervolume")
634
635    if return_series:
636        return score_series.to_frame()
637
638    # If aggregated: return joint hypervolume of valid Pareto front,
639    # or the best (least negative) violation score if none are valid
640    valid_mask = Y >= ref_point
641    all_valid_idx = valid_mask.all(dim=-1)
642    
643    if all_valid_idx.any():
644        return float(hv_calculator.compute(Y[all_valid_idx]))
645    else:
646        return float(max(scores))

Purpose:

  • Computes hypervolume for valid points and a negative penalty score for points violating at least one DVH requirement.

Inputs

- dvh_metrics: pd.DataFrame with candidate solutions as rows.
- dvh_metric_goals: dict mapping metric -> [operator ('>=' or '<='), threshold].
- return_series: If True, returns a pd.Series with scores for each individual row.
If False, returns a single float (joint HV of valid set, 
or worst negative violation if no point is valid).
class MOO_Ax(brachyutils.planning.MOO): 
 21class MOO_Ax(MOO):
 22    def __init__(
 23        self,
 24        catheter_table_optim: CatheterTableOptim_Gurobi,
 25        parameter_space: Dict[str, np.typing.ArrayLike],
 26        max_workers: int = 16,
 27        normalize = False,
 28        anchor_dvh_metric: str = None,
 29        sampler_name_id:Literal["fast", "quality", "qNEHVI"]="qNEHVI",
 30        slack_space_shrinkage: float = None,
 31        slack_objective_threshold: float | Dict[str, float] = 0,
 32        device: Literal["cpu", "cuda"] = "cpu",
 33        ):
 34        r"""
 35        ### Purpose:
 36        - Configure Ax as the backend for multi-objective optimization.
 37
 38        - For the shared optimization inputs, DVH goals, parameter-space format,
 39        and inherited behavior, see the `MOO` documentation in `moo.py`.
 40
 41        - The instance exposes the Ax `Client` as `tuner`, along with the
 42        configured sampler and objective slack values.
 43
 44        ### Inputs:
 45        The following inputs are specific to the Ax backend:
 46        - `sampler_name_id`: Ax generation strategy to use: `"fast"`,
 47            `"quality"`, or `"qNEHVI"` (default).
 48        - `device`: `"cpu"` or `"cuda"`; selects the device for Ax's
 49            BoTorch optimization when using `"qNEHVI"`.
 50        """
 51        self.tuner: Client
 52        super().__init__(
 53            catheter_table_optim= catheter_table_optim,
 54            parameter_space= parameter_space,
 55            max_workers= max_workers,
 56            normalize= normalize,
 57            anchor_dvh_metric=anchor_dvh_metric,
 58            slack_space_shrinkage=slack_space_shrinkage,
 59            slack_objective_threshold=slack_objective_threshold
 60            )
 61        self.sampler_name_id = sampler_name_id
 62        self.device = device
 63        self._ax_parameters = None
 64        self._ax_constraints = None
 65        self._ax_objectives = None
 66
 67        if self.device == "cuda":
 68            if not cuda.is_available:
 69                self.device = "cpu"
 70        # fill out the ax-specific attributes
 71        self.set_tuner()
 72
 73    def _parameter_space_to_ax(self):
 74        r"""
 75        ### Purpose:
 76        - To convert the brachy MOO parameters to ax parameters stored at
 77        `self._ax_parameters`
 78        """
 79        self._ax_parameters = []
 80        for param_space in self.parameter_space:
 81            ax_param = RangeParameterConfig(
 82                name=param_space,
 83                bounds=self.parameter_space[param_space],
 84                parameter_type="float",
 85            )
 86            self._ax_parameters.append(ax_param)
 87
 88    def set_tuner(self):
 89        self._parameter_space_to_ax()
 90        # # instantiate a new tuner object. in ax it's called Client
 91        self.tuner = Client()
 92        self.tuner.configure_experiment(parameters = self._ax_parameters)
 93        # # build the objective string
 94        ax_objectives = []
 95        outcome_constraints = []
 96        for dvh_name, direction in self.directions.items():
 97            if direction == "minimize":
 98                ax_objectives.append(
 99                    f"-{_clean_dvh_names(dvh_name)}"
100                )
101                outcome_constraints.append(
102                    f"{_clean_dvh_names(dvh_name)} <= {
103                        self.dvh_metric_goals[dvh_name][1]
104                        *(1+self.slack_objective_threshold.get(dvh_name, 0))}"
105                )
106            else:
107                ax_objectives.append(
108                    f"{_clean_dvh_names(dvh_name)}"
109                )
110                outcome_constraints.append(
111                    f"{_clean_dvh_names(dvh_name)} >= {
112                        self.dvh_metric_goals[dvh_name][1]
113                        *(1-self.slack_objective_threshold.get(dvh_name, 0))}"
114                )
115        ax_objectives = ", ".join(ax_objectives)
116        self._ax_objectives = ax_objectives
117        self._ax_constraints = outcome_constraints
118
119        self.tuner.configure_optimization(
120            objective=ax_objectives,
121            outcome_constraints=outcome_constraints
122        )
123
124    def objectives(self, parameters, sampler_name_id):
125        observed_objects = super().objectives(parameters, sampler_name_id)
126        old_columns = observed_objects.columns
127        new_columns = []
128        for col in old_columns:
129            new_columns.append(_clean_dvh_names(col))
130        observed_objects.columns = new_columns
131        return observed_objects
132
133    def run_random_sampling(
134        self,
135        n_samples,
136        use_for_warmup: bool = True
137        ):
138        self.tuner.configure_generation_strategy(
139            method="random_search",
140            initialization_budget=n_samples,)
141        trials = self.tuner.get_next_trials(max_trials=n_samples)
142        param_trials = self.get_parameters_from_trials(trials=trials)
143        objectives = self.objectives(parameters=param_trials, sampler_name_id="random_search")
144        if self.slack_space_shrinkage is not None:
145            acceptable_trials = self.shrink_parameter_space(return_acceptable_trials=True)
146            self.set_tuner()
147            true_indices = acceptable_trials.index[acceptable_trials["acceptable"]].tolist()
148            new_trials = {}
149            for i, true_indx in enumerate(true_indices):
150                new_trials[i]=trials[true_indx]
151            trials = new_trials
152        if use_for_warmup:
153            self.attach_objectives_to_trials(trials=trials, observed_objectives=objectives)
154        else:
155            self.set_tuner()
156
157    def run_trials(self, n_trials: int, batch_size: int = 1):
158        if self.sampler_name_id == "qNEHVI":
159            nodes = [
160                GenerationStep(
161                generator=Generators.SOBOL,
162                num_trials=1,),
163                GenerationStep(
164                generator=Generators.BOTORCH_MODULAR,
165                num_trials=-1,
166                model_kwargs={
167                    "botorch_acqf_class": qLogNoisyExpectedHypervolumeImprovement,
168                    "torch_device": self.device,
169                    },)
170                ]
171            self.tuner.set_generation_strategy(
172                GenerationStrategy(nodes=nodes, name=self.sampler_name_id))
173        else:
174            self.tuner.configure_generation_strategy(

182        for _ in range(n_trials):

Purpose:

  • To evaluate the objectives for the parameters generated in each trial. The objectives are the DVH metrics in the order set by the keys in self.dvh_metric_goals.
  • All parameters passed here are evaluated together in a single, batched call to evaluate_parameters(), which parallelizes the underlying Gurobi solves across self.max_workers threads.
  • Also calculates the hyper-volume and whetheter each parameter lead to acceptable dvh metrics or not.
  • Lastly, self.trial_data is updated with all the information:
    • parameter values
    • dvh metrics observed
    • hyper volume
    • acceptability

Inputs:

  • parameters := A dataframe of parameters to be evaluated. The columns are the names of the parameters while the rows are parameter values for each trial.
  • sampler_name_id: str := The name of the sampler being used. This is used to keep track of which sampler was used for each trial in the self.trial_data dataframe.

Outputs:

  • A dataframe with the dvh metrics specified by the keys in self.dvh_metric_goals.

133    def run_random_sampling(
134        self,
135        n_samples,
136        use_for_warmup: bool = True
137        ):
138        self.tuner.configure_generation_strategy(
139            method="random_search",
140            initialization_budget=n_samples,)
141        trials = self.tuner.get_next_trials(max_trials=n_samples)
142        param_trials = self.get_parameters_from_trials(trials=trials)
143        objectives = self.objectives(parameters=param_trials, sampler_name_id="random_search")
144        if self.slack_space_shrinkage is not None:
145            acceptable_trials = self.shrink_parameter_space(return_acceptable_trials=True)
146            self.set_tuner()
147            true_indices = acceptable_trials.index[acceptable_trials["acceptable"]].tolist()
148            new_trials = {}
149            for i, true_indx in enumerate(true_indices):
150                new_trials[i]=trials[true_indx]
151            trials = new_trials
152        if use_for_warmup:
153            self.attach_objectives_to_trials(trials=trials, observed_objectives=objectives)
154        else:
155            self.set_tuner()

The total number of trials evaluated across the whole run is n_trials * batch_size.
  • When batch_size == 1 this reduces to the original sequential ask/evaluate/tell loop.

  • self.trial_data: pd.DataFrame := A master dataframe containing the result of all the trials. The columns are parameter names from the keys of self.parameter_space and the dvh metric names from the keys of self.dvh_metric_goals.
